{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01EpetpvhhxeNAShJaHdfCZG","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Avon Health — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: https://www.avonhealth.com\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Avon Health is a startup founded in 2021, headquartered in New York, NY, by Maitreyee Joshi (CEO, Carnegie Mellon CS graduate, former Product Manager at PathAI). The company builds an \"AI-first\" all-in-one EMR and practice management platform targeting modern ambulatory care delivery — from solo primary care clinics to virtual care companies. The website claims \"100,000+ providers, patients, and high-growth businesses\" use the platform, though this metric combines providers, patients, and organizations, so the actual provider count is unclear and likely much smaller. Sequoia Capital is mentioned as a supporter/investor.\n     9→\n    10→Avon Health positions itself as a next-generation, cloud-based, customizable EMR for ambulatory practices across multiple specialties. The company is small — no specific employee count was found, and the product was only ONC-certified in May 2025, suggesting it is relatively early-stage. No reviews were found on Capterra, G2, or KLAS, which is consistent with a young startup that hasn't yet accumulated significant market presence in traditional EHR review channels.\n    11→\n    12→Note: There is an unrelated product called \"AvonEHR\" (avonehr.com) focused on integrative/functional medicine — this is a completely different company and product.\n    13→\n    14→## Product: Avon EMR\n    15→\n    16→CHPL IDs: 11636 (15.04.04.3227.Avon.01.00.1.250514)\n    17→\n    18→### What It Is\n    19→\n    20→Avon EMR is a cloud-based, all-in-one electronic medical record and practice management platform. It is described as \"AI-first by design\" and \"infinitely customizable\" with a modular architecture — modules can be toggled on/off depending on practice needs. The certified module appears to be the entire product (there's no indication of separate uncertified components making up a larger suite). The product is the EMR itself, which includes clinical documentation, practice management, patient engagement, and revenue cycle management all in one platform.\n    21→\n    22→The system is certified for a broad set of ONC criteria: clinical data management (a)(1)-(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14); transitions of care (b)(1)-(b)(2); care plan exchange (b)(11); clinical quality measures (c)(1)-(c)(3); patient portal/VDT (e)(1); patient health information export (e)(3); FHIR API (g)(10); and immunization registry reporting (h)(1). This breadth is consistent with a full-featured ambulatory EMR.\n    23→\n    24→### Users & Market\n    25→\n    26→**Target users**: Physicians, physician assistants, nurse practitioners (per SED description), plus practice managers and billing staff based on functionality.\n    27→\n    28→**Clinical settings**: Ambulatory care across multiple specialties — primary care, behavioral health, women's health, chronic care management, pediatrics, specialty care, hospice, and geriatrics. The vendor emphasizes serving both traditional brick-and-mortar practices and virtual/telehealth-first care delivery companies.\n    29→\n    30→**Scale**: Marketed to practices ranging from solo clinics with ~400 patients to virtual care companies with 100,000+ patients. The \"100,000+ providers, patients, and high-growth businesses\" claim on the homepage is ambiguous and likely includes patient users of the portal.\n    31→\n    32→**Notable customers**: None identified. No case studies or named customers were found on the website or in third-party sources. The vendor website includes testimonials but without identifying specific organizations.\n    33→\n    34→**Market position**: Early-stage startup. No presence on major EHR review platforms (Capterra, G2, KLAS). The recent ONC certification (May 2025) and lack of third-party reviews suggest a company still building its customer base.\n    35→\n    36→### Modules & Functionality\n    37→\n    38→The product is organized into toggleable modules documented on the vendor's guides site (guides.avonhealth.com). Based on the vendor website, documentation, and pricing page, the platform includes:\n    39→\n    40→**Clinical Documentation**\n    41→- Visit notes — clinical encounter documentation\n    42→- Care plans — treatment planning\n    43→- Documents — document storage and management\n    44→- AI Scribe — records clinician-patient interactions and auto-generates visit note drafts (Pro/Enterprise tier feature)\n    45→\n    46→**Prescriptions & Medication Management**\n    47→- E-prescribing (via integration, listed as pass-through pricing)\n    48→- Prescription fulfillment tracking\n    49→\n    50→**Laboratory & Imaging**\n    51→- Lab orders — can send to 1000+ labs across the country with parsed results returned into the platform (pass-through pricing)\n    52→- Imaging orders\n    53→- Mobile phlebotomy scheduling\n    54→- At-home test kit management\n    55→\n    56→**Scheduling**\n    57→- Virtual and in-person appointments\n    58→- One-time or recurring visits\n    59→- Individual or group sessions\n    60→- Intelligent provider matching (license type, location, availability, time zone)\n    61→- Patient self-scheduling\n    62→- Automated confirmations and reminders\n    63→- Integrated video visits\n    64→- Calendar sync with external calendars\n    65→\n    66→**Patient Engagement**\n    67→- Patient portal — view medical records, schedule appointments, message care team, complete forms, view educational content\n    68→- Caregiver portal\n    69→- Messaging — in-app, 2-way SMS, internal notes\n    70→- Forms and intake forms with embedded logic\n    71→- Courses — patient education content delivery\n    72→- SMS and email notifications\n    73→\n    74→**Practice Management & Billing**\n    75→- Revenue cycle management (pass-through pricing)\n    76→- Eligibility checks / insurance verification (pass-through pricing)\n    77→- Invoicing\n    78→- Superbills\n    79→- E-faxing (pass-through pricing)\n    80→- Payment collection\n    81→\n    82→**Analytics & Reporting**\n    83→- Real-time dashboards for clinical, operational, and financial metrics\n    84→- Filtering by provider, patient, or date\n    85→- Drill-down from KPIs to patient-level data\n    86→- Export and sharing of reports\n    87→- AI Data Analyst for insights generation (Pro/Enterprise tier)\n    88→- One certified clinical quality messages (2-way)\n   155→- Intake form submissions\n   156→- Patient education course progress\n   157→- Patient-generated data from forms\n   158→\n   159→**Financial/billing data** (evidenced by RCM Data Analyst query results\n   182→\n   183→The pricing model reveals a distinction between core platform features (included in subscription) and transactional services (e-prescribing, lab orders, eligibility checks, e-faxing, RCM) that operate on pass-through pricing. This suggests these integrations flow through third-party services but the data is stored within the Avon EMR platform.\n   184→\n   185→**Gaps/uncertainties**: The vendor website does not mention specific specialty-specific templates or content (e.g., behavioral health assessments, OB/GYN-specific forms) despite listing these as target specialties. It's unclear how deeply the product serves each listed specialty versus being a general-purpose platform. This certification does not represent an endorsement by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. Certification Criteria 170.315 (a)(1): Computerized Provider Order Entry (CPOE) - Medications 170.315 (a)(2): Computerized Provider Order Entry (CPOE) - Laboratory 170.315 (a)(3): Computerized Provider Order Entry (CPOE) - Diagnostic Imaging 170.315 (a)(4): Drug-Drug, Drug-Allergy Interaction Checks for CPOE 170.315 (a)(5): Demographics 170.315 (a)(12): Family Health History 170.315 (a)(14): Implantable Device List 170.315 (b)(1): Transitions of Care 170.315 (b)(10): Electronic Health Information Export 170.315 (b)(11): Decision Support Interventions 170.315 (c)(1): Clinical Quality Measures - Record and Export 170.315 (c)(2): Clinical Quality Measures - Import and Calculate 170.315 (c)(3): Clinical Quality Measures - Report 170.315 (d)(1): Authentication, Access Control, Authorization 170.315 (d)(2): Auditable Events and Tamper-Resistance 170.315 (d)(3): Audit Report(s) 170.315 (d)(4): Amendments 170.315 (d)(5): Automatic Access Time-out 170.315 (d)(6): Emergency Access 170.315 (d)(7): End-User Device Encryption 170.315 (d)(8): Integrity 170.315 (d)(9): Trusted Connection 170.315 (d)(12): Encrypt Authentication Credentials 170.315 (d)(13): Multi-Factor Authentication 170.315 (e)(3): Patient Health Information Capture 170.315 (g)(2): Automated Measure Calculation 170.315 (g)(3): Safety-Enhanced Design 170.315 (g)(4): Quality Management System 170.315 (g)(5): Accessibility-Centered Design 170.315 (g)(6): Consolidated CDA Creation Performance 170.315 (g)(7): Application Access - Patient Selection 170.315 (g)(9): Application Access - All Data Request 170.315 (g)(10): Standardized API for Patient and Population Services 170.315 (h)(1): Direct Project Certified Clinical Quality Measures 170.315(c)(3) — CMS2 v13: Preventive Care and Screening: Screening for Depression and Follow-up Plan Additional Software Used EMR Direct AccessGUDID Costs Users pay a monthly fee to Avon Health to access the Avon EMR based on the number of provider seats or number of patients. Users electing to use the features included under the Avon Cures Update version certification may also incur additional monthly fees. Multi-Factor Authentication MFA is required for all users accessing the system. The authentication process combines: Something the user knows: Email and password Something the user has: A one-time code sent via SMS to the user’s registered phone number Standards Version Advancement Process (SVAP) Notice Under the SVAP, the Office of the National Coordinator (ONC) for Health IT allows vendors to voluntarily update certified health IT products to use more advanced versions of standards than those adopted in ONC Certification Criteria. For its certified View, Download and Transmit functionality, Avon Health remains compliant with the WCAG versions supported by World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), in conjunction with the following Users electing to use the features included under the Avon Cures Update version certification may also incur additional monthly fees. Multi-Factor Authentication MFA is required for all users accessing the system. The authentication process combines: Something the user knows: Email and password Something the user has: A one-time code sent via SMS to the user’s registered phone number Standards Version Advancement Process (SVAP) Notice Under the SVAP, the Office of the National Coordinator (ONC) for Health IT allows vendors to voluntarily update certified health IT products to use more advanced versions of standards than those adopted in ONC Certification Criteria. Appointment types Forms Visit note templates Care plan templates Document templates Products Intake flows Smart phrases Triage team Integrations Video call integration Prescriptions integration Labs integration Imaging integration Calendar integration SMS integration Email integration Fax integration Patient payments integration Revenue cycle management integration EHI Export This document describes Avon&#x27;s support for ONC §170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information export. Per (b)(10) ONC Certification, Avon supports two types of electronic health information exports: Single patient System/patient population EHI Export What is Electronic Health Information (EHI)? Electronic Health Information (EHI) refers to electronic protected health information (ePHI) that is part of a designated record set, as defined under HIPAA. This includes: Medical and billing records about individuals maintained by or for a healthcare provider. Enrollment, payment, claims adjudication, and case or medical management records maintained by or for a health plan. Other records used, in whole or in part, to make decisions about individuals. EHI does not include psychotherapy notes as defined in 45 CFR 164.501 or information compiled in reasonable anticipation of, or for use in, a civil, criminal, or administrative action or proceeding. In short, EHI covers the same electronic health information that individuals have the right to access under the HIPAA Privacy Rule. Generating an Export An admin can initiate a single-patient export by navigating to a patient’s profile and pressing the &quot;Export EHI&quot; button. The patient population data export is handled by the Avon Support team as it depends on size of data, time and efforts required to manage the server resources. Please email support@avonhealth.com with the subject line “Patient Population b10 Export Request” to initiate the process. Export Format The EHI Export process generates a .zip file that includes CSV files, PDF documents, PNG images, and a dedicated folder for each patient. For the patient population export, the .zip file contains one directory per patient. Each directory is named using the following convention: &lt;FirstName&gt;&lt;LastName&gt;_&lt;MRN&gt; The contents of each patient directory mirror those of the individual patient export. Further details on the included files are provided below. Data Categories Included The export includes all electronic health information (EHI) that is part of the designated record set, organized into the following categories: Demographics Name Date of birth Sex Race and ethnicity Language preferences Addresses Clinical Information Allergies and adverse reactions Medications, including prescription history and active medications Problem list (diagnoses) Immunizations Family history Vital signs Procedures Surgical history Lab results Imaging results Clinical notes (e.g., progress notes, history and physical, discharge summaries) Care plans Administrative and Billing Information Appointments Insurance details Insurance claims Payment history Other Documents Forms Uploaded documents (PDFs) and images (PNGs) Next Getting started → On this page EHI Export What is Electronic Health Information (EHI)? This includes:\"]},{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"ul\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"li\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"p\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[\"Medical and billing records about individuals maintained by or for a healthcare provider.\"]}]},{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"li\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"p\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[\"Enrollment, payment, claims adjudication, and case or medical management records maintained by or for a health plan.\"]}]},{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"li\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"p\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[\"Other records used, in whole or in part, to make decisions about individuals.\"]}]}]},{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"p\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[\"EHI does not include psychotherapy notes as defined in 45 CFR 164.501 or information compiled in reasonable anticipation of, or for use in, a civil, criminal, or administrative action or proceeding.\"]},{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"p\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[\"In short, EHI covers the same electronic health information that individuals have the right to access under the HIPAA Privacy Rule.\"]},{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"h3\",\"attributes\":{\"id\":\"generating-an-export\"},\"children\":[\"Generating an Export\"]},{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"p\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[\"An admin can initiate a single-patient export by navigating to a patient’s profile and pressing the \\\"Export EHI\\\" button.\"]},{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"p\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[\"The patient population data export is handled by the Avon Support team as it depends on size of data, time and efforts required to manage the server resources. Please email support@avonhealth.com with the subject line “Patient Population b10 Export Request” to initiate the process.\"]},{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"h3\",\"attributes\":{\"id\":\"export-format\"},\"children\":[\"Export Format\"]},{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"p\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[\"The EHI Export process generates a .zip file that includes CSV files, PDF documents, PNG images, and a dedicated folder for each patient.\"]},{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"p\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[\"For the patient population export, the .zip file contains one directory per patient. Each directory is named using the following convention:\"]},{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"p\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[\"\\u003cFirstName\\u003e\\u003cLastName\\u003e_\\u003cMRN\\u003e\"]},{\"$$mdtype\":\"Tag\",\"name\":\"p\",\"attributes\":{},\"children\":[\"The contents of each patient directory mirror those of the individual patient export. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_012U3FbRYrusHedKrKZRMeTr","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01BspGMrZdFZrXUWFeB5U12B","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/avon-health--avon-emr/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Avon Health — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://avonhealth.com/meaningful-use\n- CHPL IDs: 11636 (15.04.04.3227.Avon.01.00.1.250514)\n- Certification Date: May 14, 2025\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n1. **Probed registered URL** with curl:\n   ```bash\n   curl -sI -L \"https://avonhealth.com/meaningful-use\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n   ```\n   Result: HTTP 200, `text/html; charset=utf-8`, 62,091 bytes. Next.js app hosted on Vercel.\n\n2. **Examined page content.** The page is the \"Avon Health ONC Certification\" page listing all certified criteria, costs, MFA details, SVAP notices, and two links at the bottom:\n   - \"EHI Export Documentation\" → `https://guides.avonhealth.com/docs/ehi-export`\n   - \"API Documentation\" → `https://docs.avonhealth.com`\n\n3. **Searched for downloadable files** on both the certification page and EHI export page:\n   ```bash\n   grep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\\.(pdf|zip|xlsx|xls|csv|json|doc|docx|yaml|yml)[^\"]*\"' /tmp/avon-page.html\n   grep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\\.(pdf|zip|xlsx|xls|csv|json|doc|docx|yaml|yml)[^\"]*\"' /tmp/ehi-export-page.html\n   ```\n   Result: No downloadable files found on either page.\n\n4. **Fetched and saved EHI export documentation page:**\n   ```bash\n   curl -sL \"https://guides.avonhealth.com/docs/ehi-export\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o downloads/ehi-export.html\n   ```\n   Result: 52,873 bytes of HTML (Next.js SSG page with embedded structured JSON content).\n\n5. **Took full-page screenshots** of both the certification page and the EHI export documentation page in a browser.\n\n6. **Checked API documentation site** at `https://docs.avonhealth.com`. This is a separate REST API reference site with detailed resource documentation (Patient, Allergy, Condition, Medication, etc.). However, the EHI export documentation does not reference the API as its export mechanism — the export produces a ZIP file with CSVs, PDFs, and PNGs. The API documentation is for the (g)(10) FHIR API and general REST API, not for the (b)(10) export.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe EHI export documentation lives at a single page on the Avon Health guides site: `https://guides.avonhealth.com/docs/ehi-export`. The page describes:\n\n### Export Mechanism\n- **Single patient export**: An admin navigates to a patient's profile and clicks the \"Export EHI\" button.\n- **Patient population export**: Must be requested from the Avon Support team via email to support@avonhealth.com with subject line \"Patient Population b10 Export Request\". This is handled manually as it depends on data size and server resources.\n\n### Export Format\nThe export produces a **.zip file** containing:\n- **CSV files** — structured data\n- **PDF documents** — clinical documents\n- **PNG images** — uploaded images\n- **Dedicated folder per patient** (for population exports, named `<FirstName><LastName>_<MRN>`)\n\nThe contents of each patient directory in a population export mirror those of the individual patient export.\n\n### Data Categories\nThe documentation lists data categories organized as:\n\n**Demographics**: Name, Date of birth, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Language preferences, Addresses\n\n**Clinical Information**: Allergies and adverse reactions, Medications (including prescription history and active medications), Problem list (diagnoses), Immunizations, Family history, Vital signs, Procedures, Surgical history, Lab results, Imaging results, Clinical notes (progress notes, H&P, discharge summaries), Care plans\n\n**Administrative and Billing Information**: Appointments, Insurance details, Insurance claims, Payment history\n\n**Other Documents**: Forms, Uploaded documents (PDFs) and images (PNGs)\n\n### What Is NOT Provided\n- No data dictionary with field-level definitions, data types, or column descriptions\n- No sample export files or example CSVs\n- No schema files (no XSD, JSON Schema, OpenAPI spec, DDL)\n- No documentation of the CSV file structure (column names, data types, relationships between files)\n- No documentation of how many CSV files are generated or what each one contains\n- No documentation of coded values or value sets used in the export\n- No screenshots of the export interface or example output\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nComparing against the product research, which identifies Avon EMR as a comprehensive ambulatory EMR with clinical, scheduling, messaging, billing, patient engagement, and AI features:\n\n**Clearly covered domains:**\n- Demographics (name, DOB, sex, race/ethnicity, language, addresses)\n- Problem lists / diagnoses\n- Medications and prescription history\n- Allergies and adverse reactions\n- Immunizations\n- Family history\n- Vital signs\n- Procedures and surgical history\n- Lab results\n- Imaging results\n- Clinical notes (progress notes, H&P, discharge summaries)\n- Care plans\n- Insurance details and claims\n- Payment history\n- Appointments\n- Forms (patient-submitted intake forms, etc.)\n- Uploaded documents and images\n\n**Domains mentioned in product research but absent or ambiguous in export documentation:**\n- **Messaging data** — The product has in-app messaging, 2-way SMS, and internal notes. These are not mentioned in the export.\n- **Prescriptions (e-prescribing details)** — \"Medications, including prescription history\" is listed, but it's unclear whether this includes full e-prescribing transaction data (pharmacy, fill status, etc.) or just the medication list.\n- **Superbills** — The product has a superbills feature with procedure and diagnosis codes. Not mentioned in export.\n- **Invoices** — The product generates invoices. Not explicitly mentioned in export.\n- **Eligibility checks** — Insurance eligibility data. Not mentioned.\n- **Revenue cycle management data** — The product integrates RCM. Not mentioned beyond \"insurance claims\" and \"payment history.\"\n- **Courses** — Patient education content. Not mentioned.\n- **Tasks** — Clinical task assignments. Not mentioned.\n- **Fax records** — E-faxing is a product feature. Not mentioned.\n- **Custom fields and custom objects** — The product supports custom fields/objects for extensibility. Not mentioned.\n- **AI Scribe transcriptions** — The product generates AI-powered visit note drafts. Not mentioned whether transcriptions or AI-generated content are included.\n- **Implantable device list** — Certified under (a)(14) but not listed in export categories.\n- **Clinical decision support data** — Certified under (a)(2). Not mentioned.\n- **Smoking status** — A standard clinical data element. Not mentioned.\n\nThe export claims to cover \"all electronic health information (EHI) that is part of the designated record set,\" which is promising language. However, the documentation only lists broad categories without field-level detail, making it impossible to verify what's actually included. Notably, several patient-facing data domains (messaging, superbills, invoices, custom data) are absent from the listed categories.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses a **vendor-proprietary format**: a ZIP file containing CSV files, PDFs, and PNGs. This is not a recognized standard (not FHIR, C-CDA, or any other interoperability format), but it's a reasonable approach for a (b)(10) export — CSVs are human-readable and machine-processable, and including original documents as PDFs/PNGs preserves fidelity.\n\nHowever, the documentation provides **no detail on the CSV structure**. Without knowing:\n- How many CSV files are generated\n- What columns each CSV contains\n- What data types and formats are used\n- How relationships between entities are expressed (e.g., linking a lab result to a visit)\n- What coded values are used\n\n...a third party could not reliably reconstruct the patient record from the export. They would receive a ZIP file and have to reverse-engineer the CSV structure.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is **minimal**. It occupies a single web page with approximately 300 words of substantive content. It correctly explains what EHI is, describes two export types (single patient and population), and lists data categories at a high level.\n\nHowever, it lacks:\n- **Field-level documentation**: No data dictionary, no column definitions, no data types\n- **Worked examples**: No sample export files or example records\n- **Schema documentation**: No formal specification of the CSV file format\n- **Export interface documentation**: No screenshots or step-by-step guide\n- **Value set documentation**: No description of coded fields or their permissible values\n- **Relationship documentation**: No description of how CSV files relate to each other\n\nA developer could not implement an import of this data based solely on the documentation. They would need access to an actual export file to understand the structure.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\nThe documentation provides **category-level granularity only** — it tells you that \"Lab results\" are included but not what fields a lab result record contains. This is the minimum viable documentation for a (b)(10) export: it confirms the vendor has thought about what data to include, but it doesn't provide the technical detail needed to understand or use the export.\n\nThere is no versioning or change history. The documentation appears to be a single static page created for certification purposes.\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nAvon Health is an early-stage startup (certified May 2025) that has created genuine (b)(10) export documentation — this is not a repackaged FHIR API or a (g)(10)/(b)(10) conflation. The export is clearly a distinct mechanism (ZIP with CSVs) separate from their REST/FHIR API. The documentation correctly defines EHI scope and lists reasonable data categories.\n\nHowever, the documentation is thin. The absence of a data dictionary, schema, or sample export means the documentation functions as a high-level description of what the export includes, not a technical specification of how it works. For a recently certified startup, this is not unusual, but it represents a significant gap for anyone trying to understand or import the exported data.\n\nThe population export requiring manual email request to the support team (rather than a self-service mechanism) is notable — it suggests the export infrastructure is not yet fully automated.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://avonhealth.com/meaningful-use\n- EHI Export Documentation URL: https://guides.avonhealth.com/docs/ehi-export\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (content fully accessible via curl; Next.js SSG with content in HTML)\n- Navigation complexity: one_click (certification page links directly to EHI export docs)\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\nNone. The URL was live, the documentation page loaded cleanly, and all content was accessible without JavaScript rendering (the Next.js page uses SSG with all content embedded in the HTML source).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":245,"cache_read_input_tokens":55964,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":245},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7f873ebf-8735-4411-9f47-a247bf5772c9","uuid":"f37c20fd-5380-4e87-8a6d-46be6388adc0"}
